waiahole_beach_park: Waiāhole Beach Park is located on the windward coast of O‘ahu along Kaneohe Bay.
Swimming in Waiāhole Beach Park isn't possible due to the ocean bottom being shallow and the presence of a reef.
Mokoli‘i Island can be seen from Waiāhole Beach Park.
Both the Ko‘olau mountain range and Kaneohe Bay are visible from Waiāhole Beach Park.
Waiāhole Beach Park is popular for fishing, picnics, short walks, and bay views.
lyon_arboretum: The Lyon Arboretum is an public arboretum and botanical garden.
The Lyon Arboretum is located in the upper end of Mānoa Valley in O‘ahu.
The Lyon Arboretum is the only university-owned botanical garden in the United States, managed by the University of Hawaii at Mānoa.
The Lyon Arboretum has more than 6,000 tropical and subtropical plants across its 193.5 acres.
The Lyon Arboretum has over 7 miles of hiking trails.
kapolei: As of 2026, Kapolei has a population of 24,844 people.
Kapolei is known as the 'second city' of O‘ahu.
The name 'Kapolei' originates from the phrase 'Pu‘u o Kapolei,' meaning 'hill of beloved Kapo'. Kapo was a sister of Pele.
Established in July 2000, Kapolei High School is the newest traditional high school on O‘ahu.
In 1879, Kapolei was used as sugarcane and pineapple plantations by an industrialist named James Campbell.
